# Using the Starter Template {#sec-starter-template}

::: {.callout-note title="Why this matters"}
The template gives every team the same layout and a couple of pieces
(a database-connection stub, report/slide skeletons) already wired up, so
you spend Day 1 morning on data, not project setup.
:::

## Folder structure

- `src/` — your R script files. Ships with `main.R`, which stubs out a
  `connect_to_db()` function for you to implement.
- `data/` — intermediate computed datasets you save as you go.
- `docs/` — your Quarto files: `report.qmd` (written report) and
  `slides.qmd` (presentation) — see @sec-quarto.
- `_docs/` — generated automatically when you render (set as the
  `output-dir` in `_quarto.yml`). This holds your final rendered report and
  slides — commit and push it, since it's what organisers see.
- `manual/` — reference material from organisers.

Following this layout isn't mandatory, but it's what lets organisers find
your work quickly — worth it for the Professional Communication judging
pillar.

## Get set up

1. Clone your team's repo (@sec-git-github).
2. Open it in RStudio/Positron.
3. Install the packages the template uses: `dplyr`, `mongolite`, `here`.
4. Open `src/main.R` and implement `connect_to_db()` using your Atlas
   connection string (@sec-mongodb-connect) — read it with `Sys.getenv()`,
   never hardcode it.

## Use your script from a `.qmd`

Don't copy-paste code between `src/main.R` and your `.qmd` files — source it
instead. `docs/report.qmd` already does this at the top:

```r
source(here::here("src/main.R"))
```

`here::here()` keeps file paths working no matter which file you render
from — always reference files this way rather than relative paths like
`"../src/main.R"`.

For more selective imports, `box::use()` is also available if you're
already familiar with it — optional, not required.

## Fill in the report and slides

1. `docs/report.qmd` — starts as `format: html` only. Both HTML **and**
   PDF are required, so add a `pdf:` entry to the YAML before you submit
   (@sec-quarto shows the format block and PDF setup). Set your team name in
   the title too.
2. `docs/slides.qmd` — already set to `format: revealjs`. A finished deck is
   required from every team, not just finalists — only the 5 finalists
   present it live, but everyone submits one (@sec-quarto covers building
   slides).

## Render everything

From the project root:

```bash
quarto render
```

This renders every `.qmd` under `docs/` and writes the output into
`_docs/`.

## Submit

There's no file to zip or upload — organisers submit by cloning your
repository directly.

1. Run `quarto render` so `_docs/` is up to date.
2. Commit and push everything, including `_docs/` (@sec-git-github) —
   unlike a typical build folder, this one needs to be pushed, since it's
   your actual submitted report and slides.
3. Confirm the repo is public and the final push landed before the
   deadline.
